From e0a1284b293bdf91a68a6d1a0479ad476d0d8ec2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Gow <davidgow@google.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Feb 2024 17:27:17 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] time/kunit: Use correct format specifier

'days' is a s64 (from div_s64), and so should use a %lld specifier.

This was found by extending KUnit's assertion macros to use gcc's
__printf attribute.

Fixes: 276010551664 ("time: Improve performance of time64_to_tm()")
Signed-off-by: David Gow <davidgow@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240221092728.1281499-5-davidgow@google.com

diff --git a/kernel/time/time_test.c b/kernel/time/time_test.c
index ca058c8af6ba..3e5d422dd15c 100644
--- a/kernel/time/time_test.c
+++ b/kernel/time/time_test.c
@@ -73,7 +73,7 @@ static void time64_to_tm_test_date_range(struct kunit *test)
 
 		days = div_s64(secs, 86400);
 
-		#define FAIL_MSG "%05ld/%02d/%02d (%2d) : %ld", \
+		#define FAIL_MSG "%05ld/%02d/%02d (%2d) : %lld", \
 			year, month, mdday, yday, days
 
 		KUNIT_ASSERT_EQ_MSG(test, year - 1900, result.tm_year, FAIL_MSG);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `kernel/time/time_test.c`**
   - The format specifier in the `FAIL_MSG` macro was changed from `%ld` to `%lld` to correctly handle the `s64` type of the variable `days`, which is derived from the `div_s64` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `time_test.c` addresses a type mismatch issue by ensuring that the format specifier used for printing the `days` variable matches its data type (`s64`). This change was prompted by the extension of KUnit's assertion macros to utilize GCC's `__printf` attribute, which helps in identifying such discrepancies. The fix is linked to a previous commit that aimed to improve the performance of the `time64_to_tm()` function, indicating that the original code may not have accounted for the correct data type handling in its assertions.


This mismatch can lead to incorrect output or runtime errors, as the format specifier does not match the actual data type of the variable.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define FAIL_MSG "%05ld/%02d/%02d (%2d) : %lld", \
```
Reason:
